**Design (H = 60).** The 4×4 board has exactly 10 winning lines (4 rows, 4 columns, 2 long diagonals). For each line I built 6 ReLU units:

- **m1, m2, m3**: fire when the line holds 1 / 2 / 3 of *my* pieces and **none** of the opponent's (weights +1 on my cells, −5 on theirs suppress blocked lines). m3 ⇒ I can win by playing the line's single empty cell.
- **o2, o3**: fire when the opponent has 2 / 3 clean in the line ⇒ I must block (o3) or defuse a developing threat / prevent a fork (o2 — a cell shared by two opponent open-twos gets a doubled bonus, automatically outranking everything except a win or a forced block).
- **E**: fires when the line is completely untouched ( encourages spreading play into fresh lines, which keeps fork chances alive).

Each unit's output is routed in W2 to **every cell of its line**; since occupied cells are skipped automatically, only the playable cell collects the bonus. Second-layer weights set the priority ladder (effective per-line scores):

| pattern | score |
|---|---|
| complete my 4th (m3) | ≈ 507 |
| block opponent's 3-in-line (o3) | ≈ 55.7 |
| take a fork cell of two opponent open-2s | 3.8 |
| create my own 3-in-line threat (m2) | 3.0 |
| defuse a single opponent open-2 | 1.9 |
| build on my open single line (m1) | 0.5 |
| develop a fresh empty line | 0.15 |

A cell in several good lines sums its bonuses, so double-threat creation (2×3.0) beats fork prevention, fork prevention beats a single threat, a forced block beats everything except an immediate win, etc. b2 holds tiny tie-break priors (inner 2×2 > corners > edges) so the opening and dead positions resolve sensibly (opens at cell 5).
